reproduction_target: Reproduce, from the ONT PromethION raw reads of a single Dermacentor reticulatus female, the chromosome-scale nuclear genome assembly (basecalling, contamination screening, read filtering, Flye unguided assembly, NtLink/RagTag guided scaffolding against D. silvarum GCA_013339745.2, TGS-GapCloser gap filling, racon polishing, NCBI FCS screening), the assembly QC metrics (BUSCO arachnida_odb10, Jellyfish genome-size estimate), repeat masking (RepeatMasker + Repbase + RepeatModeler), structural annotation (liftoff / BRAKER / GALBA + AUGUSTUS, tRNAscan-SE) and its BUSCO protein assessment, nucleotide and gene synteny (minimap2 + PyCircos; jcvi/MCScan), OrthoFinder orthology and species tree, InterProScan functional annotation with the Pfam/GO fold-change enrichment and REVIGO summary, and the separate mitochondrial genome assembly (DIAMOND read recruitment, seqtk, Flye --genome-size 15k, MitoZ) plus the Ixodida mitochondrial MAFFT + IQ-TREE phylogeny. Tick collection by flagging, DNA extraction and QC, and ONT library preparation and sequencing are out of scope (W).
granularity_note: One step per named tool/analysis invocation in the Methods prose of the bioRxiv v1 full text (JATS XML returned 403 to WebFetch and to curl; the v1 .full HTML was fetched with curl at 200 and converted to text, and contains the complete Methods, Declarations and Availability sections). 33 computational steps, 3 wet-lab steps. Stage-1 prose triage only: no code was read line-by-line and nothing was executed. The stated pipeline repository (https://github.com/MatthewHiggins2017/DenovoAssemblyTools) landing page, README prose and top-level file listing were read to record the environment CLAIM; three environment specification files (Containers/FLYE.yml, Containers/FLYE.def, Setup/DeNovoAssembly.yml) were opened to classify capture_claim correctly, but no workflow/analysis source (NF/*.nf, src/*.py) was evaluated. The repository covers only the assembly and assembly-QC steps (C2-C12); every downstream step (repeat masking, annotation, synteny, orthology, functional annotation, mitochondrion, phylogeny) has no deposited code.

steps.label: Field collection of a single D. reticulatus female by flagging in an established area in Devon, England (March 2024), with morphological species identification

Sample homogenisation and high molecular weight DNA extraction (Dynabeads SILANE Genomic DNA Kit), with Qubit dsDNA HS quantification and Agilent 4200 TapeStation Genomic DNA ScreenTape QC (80% of DNA peaking at 20,000 bp)
ONT library preparation with the Ligation Sequencing Kit V14 (SQK-LSK114) and sequencing on an R10.4.1 PromethION flow cell (FLO-PRO114M)
Basecalling of raw ONT signal with Dorado v0.9.1, 'super high accuracy model' (exact model string not given) and --trim to remove adaptors
Taxonomic assignment of raw ONT reads and contamination report with Kraken2 v2.1.3; no Kraken2 database name, build date or size is stated
Removal of reads matching 'Archaea' in the Kraken2 report using KrakenTools extract_kraken_reads.py (no version stated)
Scrubbing of poor-quality and chimeric reads with yacrd v1.0.0 (no parameters stated)
Read filtering with chopper v0.6.0 to a minimum length of 1000 and minimum quality of 12
Unguided de novo assembly with Flye v2.9.2; read error values 0.04, 0.06 and 0.08 trialled, 0.06 selected on the basis of the highest BUSCO score
Guided scaffolding against the D. silvarum genome (GCA_013339745.2) with NtLink v1.3.9, maximum gap 500 and gap-fill option enabled
Improvement of the guided assembly with RagTag v2.1.0 (subcommand and parameters not stated)
Gap filling with TGS-GapCloser v1.2.1 (parameters not stated)
Polishing of the unguided and guided assemblies with racon v1.5.0 (number of rounds and parameters not stated)
Contaminant and adaptor screening with the NCBI Foreign Contamination Screen (FCS) suite; no FCS version and no GX database build stated
Assembly completeness assessment with BUSCO v5.8.2 (-m genome -l arachnida_odb10) after each pipeline stage; the arachnida_odb10 dataset is not pinned to a dated release
Approximate genome size estimation with Jellyfish v2.3.1 using 21-mers; no code deposited for this step, and no downstream model (GenomeScope or equivalent) named

Repeat identification and classification with RepeatMasker v4.1.7 against the Repbase database (Eukaryota and Arthropoda, 2018-10-26), then combined hard- and soft-masking with RepeatMasker using the RepeatModeler output
De novo repeat modelling with RepeatModeler v2.0.1 (parameters, including whether LTRStruct was enabled, not stated)
Homology-based annotation transfer with liftoff v1.6.3; the source assembly and source GFF used for the lift-over are not stated, and this approach was trialled but not used for the final annotation
Ab initio / evidence-based annotation with BRAKER v3.0.8 (protein or RNA evidence input, mode and parameters not stated); trialled and compared, but not used for the final annotation

Final structural annotation with GALBA v1.0.11, which used 'protein sequences of closely related Dermacentor sp' to train AUGUSTUS (no AUGUSTUS version, no accession list or FASTA for the training protein set, no parameters)
tRNA annotation with tRNAscan-SE (no version, no mode flag such as -E, no parameters)
Annotation completeness assessment with BUSCO v5.8.2 (-m protein -l arachnida_odb10) for the unguided and guided D. reticulatus annotations and the comparator Dermacentor assemblies

Whole-genome alignment of the masked D. reticulatus assemblies against D. silvarum with minimap2 v2.28 (-ax asm5), filtering of mapped regions to MAPQ > 60, and construction of a 'links' file (no script, no link-file format or aggregation rule given)
Nucleotide-level synteny visualisation with the PyCircos package v3.10.0 (https://github.com/ponnhide/pyCircos); no plotting script or configuration deposited
Gene-level pairwise synteny search and macrosynteny visualisation with jcvi and MCScan (Python version); no versions, no parameters, no script

Orthology inference with OrthoFinder v2.5.5 (-M msa with default mafft, -T iqtree) over the two D. reticulatus proteomes and nine public tick proteomes (GCF_038994185.2, GCA_023375885.3, GCF_013339745.2, GCA_013339765.2, GCF_016920785.2, GCA_013358835.2, GCF_037126465.1, GCF_013339725.1, GCF_013339695.2)

Functional annotation of predicted proteins with InterProScan 5.73-104.0 using 'inbuilt databases' (member-database versions not enumerated beyond the InterProScan release), E-value < 1E-30; domains of interest identified at E-value < 1E-10

Pfam-domain abundance counting and fold-change analysis between the Dermacentor genus and three comparator groups (other ticks; blood-feeding insects GCF_002204515.2, GCF_943734735.2, GCF_035046485.1; non-blood-feeding arachnids GCF_000671375.1, GCF_043381705.1), median fold-change > 2 threshold, mapping of Pfam IDs to GO terms and median fold-change per GO term. No software, script, Pfam-to-GO mapping file version, or normalisation rule (per proteome size?) is named
GO-term summarisation and visualisation with REVIGO (web service; no version, no similarity threshold, no species/GO database release, no input/output files deposited)

BLAST of predicted D. reticulatus amino acid sequences against the Dermanyssus gallinae transcriptome to predict presence/absence of heme biosynthesis pathway proteins; BLAST flavour, version, database accession and E-value threshold for this specific search are not stated

Mitochondrial read recruitment: DIAMOND v2.1.11 database built from mitochondrial amino acid sequences extracted from D. silvarum GCA_013339745.2, filtered reads searched against it at E-value < 1e-5 (extraction procedure for the reference mitochondrial proteins not described)
Sorting and deduplication of recruited mitochondrial reads with seqtk (no version, no subcommand, no parameters)
Mitochondrial genome assembly with Flye v2.9.2 (--genome-size 15k), yielding a single circular contig
Mitochondrial genome annotation with MitoZ v3.6 (clade/genetic-code options and mode not stated), producing the 15,103 bp / 38-gene mitogenome

Alignment of all Ixodida mitochondrial sequences downloaded from the NCBI Organelle database (accessed March 2025; no accession list, no query definition, no download snapshot) with MAFFT v7.525 (algorithm and parameters not stated), followed by maximum-likelihood tree inference with IQ-TREE v2.3.6 (-B 1000 -m MFP -T AUTO) and visualisation with iTOL

headline.static_readiness: 0/33 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification). Unexecuted; the declared environment (per-tool pinned conda YAMLs + Singularity definition files in the pipeline repository) is a static claim, not verified as the environment that produced the results. n_exact_capture_unexecuted = 0, n_fetch_required = 10.
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 0/33 (0%) readiness upper bound at stage 1: (n_R + n_RI) / |S| = (0 + 0) / 33. The binding constraint is the data axis, which is 0 for every single computational step: the availability statement reads verbatim 'All raw sequencing data have been submitted and genome assemblies and annotations have been submitted to NCBI (Accessions TBC) and LSHTM genomics data repository: https://genomics.lshtm.ac.uk/data/.' No accession is given for the ONT reads, the two assemblies, the annotations or the mitogenome, and the LSHTM link is a repository root rather than a deposit, so no input to any step is retrievable. Method reporting is otherwise unusually strong for this genre - 24 of 33 steps carry an exact prose version pin and the assembly half is backed by a public Nextflow/Singularity pipeline with fully pinned conda environment files - so this paper would move substantially once accessions are released. Unexecuted; under-claims by construction.

gaps.where: Availability of data and materials - every computational step C1-C33
gaps.missing: No accession exists for any dataset produced by this study. Verbatim: 'All raw sequencing data have been submitted and genome assemblies and annotations have been submitted to NCBI (Accessions TBC) and LSHTM genomics data repository: https://genomics.lshtm.ac.uk/data/.' The ONT raw reads (input to C1-C6, C29-C31), the unguided and guided assemblies, the repeat-masked assemblies, the GALBA annotations and proteomes (input to C20-C28), and the 15,103 bp mitogenome are all 'TBC'. The LSHTM URL is a directory root with no per-dataset landing page or identifier. This sets data = 0 on all 33 computational steps and is the single dominant blocker of the assessment.
gaps.how_to_close: Release the SRA/BioProject accession for the ONT run and the GenBank/GCA accessions for both assemblies and their annotations, and replace the repository root URL with a per-dataset landing page or DOI.

gaps.missing: The only code cited in the paper is the assembly pipeline at https://github.com/MatthewHiggins2017/DenovoAssemblyTools, whose Nextflow modules cover raw-data QC, contig assembly, guided/unguided scaffolding, gap closing, polishing, foreign contamination screening and assembly assessment - i.e. steps C2-C12 only. There is no deposited code for genome-size estimation, repeat masking and modelling, any of the three annotation routes, the minimap2 link-file construction, PyCircos plotting, jcvi/MCScan synteny, OrthoFinder, InterProScan post-processing, the Pfam/GO fold-change analysis, the heme-pathway BLAST, the mitochondrial assembly and annotation, or the Ixodida phylogeny. The paper does not state that the repository covers only part of the analysis.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the downstream analysis scripts (or the full command log) in the same repository and state explicitly which stages the cited pipeline does and does not cover.

gaps.missing: The pipeline is cited by bare repository URL with no commit SHA, no tag and no archival DOI. The repository does carry a tag/release v0.0.1, but the paper points at the mutable default branch, so the exact pipeline state used for this assembly is not recoverable. The repository also carries no LICENSE file, which leaves reuse rights undefined.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite the tag or a Zenodo/Software Heritage archive of the exact pipeline state used, and add a license.

gaps.where: C2 (Kraken2 DB), C11 (NCBI FCS GX DB), C12/C20 (BUSCO arachnida_odb10), C14 (Repbase), C18 (Dermacentor training proteins), C25 (InterProScan member databases), C27 (REVIGO GO release), C28 (D. gallinae transcriptome), C33 (NCBI Organelle download)
gaps.missing: Reference resources are consumed without pinned releases. The Kraken2 database is not named at all; the FCS GX database build is not stated; the BUSCO arachnida_odb10 lineage set is given without its dated release; InterProScan member-database versions are covered only by the 5.73-104.0 release string; REVIGO's underlying GO release and similarity setting are unstated; the D. gallinae transcriptome has no accession; the NCBI Organelle download is pinned only by the phrase 'Accessed: March 2025' with no accession list or query string, so the 189-genome comparison set cannot be reconstructed. Repbase is the one positive case - it is pinned as 'Eukaryota and Arthropoda, 2018-10-26' - but Repbase is license-gated, so obtaining that exact snapshot requires a subscription. No workflow file was read at stage 1, so none of these fetches can be classified as class A.
gaps.how_to_close: State database names, builds and download dates with checksums; deposit the NCBI Organelle accession list and the GALBA training protein FASTA as supplementary files.

gaps.missing: Nine tools are named without any version string, in a Methods section that otherwise pins versions exactly (Dorado v0.9.1, Kraken2 v2.1.3, yacrd v1.0.0, chopper v0.6.0, Flye v2.9.2, NtLink v1.3.9, RagTag v2.1.0, TGS-GapCloser v1.2.1, racon v1.5.0, BUSCO v5.8.2, Jellyfish v2.3.1, RepeatMasker v4.1.7, RepeatModeler v2.0.1, liftoff v1.6.3, BRAKER v3.0.8, GALBA v1.0.11, minimap2 v2.28, PyCircos v3.10.0, OrthoFinder v2.5.5, InterProScan 5.73-104.0, DIAMOND v2.1.11, MitoZ v3.6, MAFFT v7.525, IQ-TREE v2.3.6). Separately, exact prose pins alone do not constitute environment closure: the version axis is therefore capped at 1 for every step at stage 1, and the environment closure that does exist (Containers/*.yml, Containers/*.def, Setup/DeNovoAssembly.yml in the pipeline repository) is not mentioned anywhere in the paper.
gaps.how_to_close: Add the nine missing version strings, and reference the pipeline's container definitions / conda environment files from the Methods so the closure claim is discoverable from the paper.

gaps.missing: Several steps are described at a level that does not determine the computation. liftoff v1.6.3 is run with no stated source assembly or source GFF. BRAKER v3.0.8 is run with no stated evidence input or mode. GALBA is trained on unnamed 'protein sequences of closely related Dermacentor sp'. The minimap2 output is 'filtered to retain high-quality matches (MAPQ>60) ... and were used to create a links file' with no script and no aggregation rule. The Pfam/GO enrichment defines a median fold-change > 2 cutoff but no normalisation for proteome size, no multiple-testing treatment and no tool. The mitochondrial DIAMOND database is built from 'mitochondrial amino acid sequences extracted from the D. silvarum assembly' without describing the extraction. In addition, model selection across the three annotation routes is stated qualitatively ('GALBA yielded the best results') without the comparison metric table for liftoff.
gaps.how_to_close: State each tool's inputs and full command line, and deposit the post-processing scripts for the links file and the Pfam/GO fold-change analysis.

gaps.missing: Figure-producing steps run through interactive web services (REVIGO for GO summarisation, iTOL for both the OrthoFinder species tree and the Ixodida mitochondrial tree) with no saved session, no configuration export and no input/output files. The PyCircos circos plot has no deposited plotting script. These figures cannot be regenerated from the paper.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the REVIGO input table and settings, the iTOL tree files plus annotation/config files, and the PyCircos plotting script.
